newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Zinny couldn't give a toss what ACT say!.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Zinny couldn't give a toss what ACT say!.

text.p: AUCKLAND, May 29 - Since the weekend Auckland have heard all the talk from across the Tasman about how much the ACT Brumbies have to gain and the Blues to lose in Saturday's Super 12 rugby final at Eden Park.
But Blues captain Zinzan Brooke says he couldn't care less what the Brumbies have been saying, NZPA reports.
The fact the Blues stand on the threshold of completing a remarkable feat of going through the season unbeaten is spur enough.
"In some games the motivation has to come from within because you feel flat but in a game like this the occasion takes care of itself," Brooke said.
"Our trainings have been intense this week.
"We just can't afford to hold anything back now because it is the last game. There are a few jitters among the side and the encouraging thing is the enthusiasm is very good."
The Blues were creating a monster opposition, setting a standard they needed to reach beyond anything else this season.
"It is going to be a big match-up. It is going to be a big test for a lot of individuals," Brooke said.
"There could be guys being found out about their defensive and attacking roles. We just have to wait on the day to see how individuals go.
"Finals rugby is just something different and sometimes it can do funny things to players."
Ironically it was the final quarter against Natal last weekend, when the South Africans ran in a swag of tries, that is providing the needle for the Blues.
"We need to improve in the last 20 minutes obviously. There was a lot of focus there in the game against Natal but everyone forgets the game was well gone by then," Brooke said.
"It was gone by halftime when it was 35-5. We said then that we wanted to score first in the second half and then shut up shop. I think we shut up shop too soon and forgot to tell the Natal people."
He is mindful too that ACT have the mettle to back their confident claims.
"The thing that sticks out in my mind is that the ACT Brumbies have won well away from home like they did against the Hurricanes in Wellington," he said.
"They know they can win well and that makes a difference."
The Blues are wary too of the key areas where the Brumbies outplayed the Hurricanes last week -- in the loose and at the restarts.
"They've got very experienced players in Troy Coker and Owen Finnegan at looseforward. And Brett Robinson is obviously a key link man so we've got to watch those guys," the Blues No 8 said.
"Coker is a very good player and it would be fair to say that we might see him back in the Australian colours because he's been one of the guys whose been consistent.
"We're confident with our restarts because Robin (Brooke) and Leo (Lafaiali'i) have gone very well there for us this year."
A severe dressing down from coach Graham Henry has produced a dramatic rise in intensity and concentration at the Blues' training this week.
There has also been a noticeably harder edge, something that has been missing since the Blues pipped the Wellington Hurricanes three weeks ago 45-42.
Teams:

Auckland Blues: Adrian Cashmore, Joeli Vidiri, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Ofisa Tonu'u, Zinzan Brooke (captain), Mark Carter, Robin Brooke, Leo Lafaiali'i, Michael Jones, Olo Brown, Sean Fitzpatrick, Craig Dowd.

ACT Brumbies: Stephen Larkham, Mitch Hardy, James Holbeck, Joe Roff, Pat Howard, David Knox, George Gregan, Troy Coker, Brett Robinson (captain), David Giffin, John Langford, Owen Finnegan, Ewen McKenzie, Marco Caputo, Patricio Noriega.
